summary: The 5-colour strand skeleton, the 15 s palette-crossfade cycle and all four dials are reproduced faithfully, but the twinkle itself is inverted and ~90x too dense — the original blinks single pixels momentarily BLACK and pulses the whole strip to 4x every ~33 s, while the port keeps ~14 pixels of 60 glowing 4x brighter at all times and never flashes globally.
observations: Both sides render cleanly on the default rig (strip, 60 px), no compile or runtime errors, on seeds 1 / 7 / 1234 and at 5/10/20/40 fps.

STRAND SKELETON MATCHES. Both sides paint exactly 5 fixed colour groups whose pixel membership never changes; at 60 px both produce group sizes 14/13/12/11/10, at 12 px orig 3/3/2/2/2 vs port 4/3/2/2/1, at 300 px orig 62/61/60/59/58 vs port 67/61/61/56/55 — so the original's strand assignment is a deterministic near-balanced spread while the port's is genuinely random; the two only coincide at the default 60 px.

PALETTE: 3 of 5 entries match, 2 do not. Held palette with sliderAutoFadePalettes=0, scaled to 255 (raw base cap is 63 on both sides): orig {red 255,0,0 | green 4,255,0 | blue 0,8,255 | deep-orange 255,45,0 | red-pink 255,0,77} vs port {red 255,0,0 | green 0,255,0 | blue 0,0,255 | amber 255,138,0 | magenta 255,0,231}. Red/green/blue agree to within quantisation; the port's warm strand is far too yellow (hue 32 deg vs 11 deg) and its pink strand is far too purple (hue 306 deg vs 342 deg).

PALETTE FADE MIDPOINT: with sliderManualPaletteSelect swept 0..1 at 0.05 steps (AutoFade=0), the original's deep-orange strand fades through a NEUTRAL GREY (raw 24,19,24 at v=0.65, i.e. ~98,78,98 of 255) and back; the port's amber strand never dips at all — its minimum over the whole sweep is raw 51,36,14 and at v=0.65 it sits at raw 57,46,33, a bright warm cream. The other four strands' fade shapes and phase groupings match (green+blue dip near v=0.35, red dips near v=0.65 on both sides).

CROSSFADE CYCLE MATCHES AT DEFAULT. Per-strand crossfade period measured by autocorrelation of meanG/meanB: orig 15.2 s, port 15.0 s (untouched). Both sides run the 5 strands phase-locked to one another with the same relative offsets. Both are fps-invariant (identical meanBrightness avg 21.6 orig / 40.7 port at 5, 10, 20 and 40 fps) — no frame-rate coupling on either side.

TWINKLE CHARACTER IS INVERTED — the headline divergence. Measured over a 400-frame 20 fps dump at untouched defaults, counting pixels whose colour deviates from its own strand's current colour: ORIG 0.16 deviant px/frame, of which 0.00 are brighter than the strands and 0.16 are dimmer, onset rate ~189/min, mean event duration 0.05 s (a single frame). PORT 15.4 deviant px/frame, of which 13.9 are BRIGHTER (up to raw 254 against a strand base of 63, i.e. 4x) and 1.6 dimmer, onset rate ~1533/min, mean event duration 0.61 s. So the original's twinkle is a rare one-frame blackout of one bulb; the port's is a quarter of the strip sustaining a bright flare.

ORIGINAL HAS A PERIODIC WHOLE-STRIP FLASH THE PORT LACKS ENTIRELY. Over a 240 s survey the original's mean brightness spikes from ~21 to 67-84 at t = 0.2, 33.2, 66.4, 99.4, 132.4, 165.4, 198.2, 231.2 s — a clean 33.0 s cadence. A --dump through one flash (t=33.0/33.2/33.4/33.6/34.0) shows ALL 60 pixels ramping together by the same ~4x factor over ~0.6 s and back, still with exactly 5 distinct colours: the boost is global/synchronous, not per pixel. The port shows zero such events in 240 s (max mean brightness 54 against a median of 41).

The flash is driven by sliderTwinkles on the original, not by a separate timer: global flashes/min = 0.0 at Twinkles=0, 3.0 at 0.5, 10.5 at 1 (~2/min untouched). The port's flash count is 0.0 at every one of those settings.

BRIGHTNESS: the port is ~1.9x too bright at defaults (mean 40.7 vs 21.6 over 60 s). With Twinkles=0 the gap shrinks to 1.24x (25.7 vs 20.7), so most of the excess is the twinkle flares; the residual ~24% is the palette difference (the port's amber and magenta strands carry more total energy than the original's deep-orange and red-pink).

STEADY STATE IS FINE ON BOTH. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both sides over 120 s and 240 s windows; the original keeps flashing on cadence to t=231 s and the port keeps twinkling at constant density — neither side decays, freezes or saturates.
CONTROL SURFACE MATCHES EXACTLY: both sides expose sliderCycleTime, sliderTwinkles, sliderAutoFadePalettes, sliderManualPaletteSelect, all kind 'slider', same labels.
Untouched-default renders differ in exactly the ways listed above (they are not an artefact of leaving dials alone) — every finding reproduces under explicit matched dial settings.

dials.name: sliderCycleTime
dials.origEffect: Sets the strand crossfade period: 5.6 s at 0, 20.6 s at 0.5, 34.5 s at 1 (autocorrelation of meanB, Twinkles pinned to 0). Untouched default renders at 15.2 s.
dials.portEffect: Same axis and direction but a shifted range: 3.0 s at 0, 16.5 s at 0.5, 30.6 s at 1. Untouched default renders at 15.0 s, so the defaults agree while the dial's low end runs ~1.9x too fast and the high end ~11% too fast.

dials.name: sliderTwinkles
dials.origEffect: 0 = strands breathe with no twinkles at all (max mean brightness 23, motion 0). Raising it increases the rate of whole-strip 4x flashes (0 / 3.0 / 10.5 per minute at 0 / 0.5 / 1) and of momentary single-pixel blackouts. No pixel ever gets brighter than its strand except during a global flash.
dials.portEffect: 0 = identical quiet strand breathing (matches). Raising it increases the number of INDIVIDUAL pixels boosted up to 4x: 0 bright px at 0, 3-21 px >100 at 0.5, dense per-pixel flicker with up to 45 distinct colours at 1. Never produces a whole-strip flash at any value.

dials.name: sliderAutoFadePalettes
dials.origEffect: Gates the crossfade: at 0 and 0.5 the 5 strand colours are frozen for the whole 90 s window (motion 0); at 1 they crossfade on the CycleTime period.
dials.portEffect: Identical gating with the same threshold — frozen at 0 and 0.5, fading at 1.

dials.name: sliderManualPaletteSelect
dials.origEffect: Inert while AutoFadePalettes is on (this is why the 4 s probe reported it inert on both sides — a false inert). With AutoFade=0 it is fully live: sweeping 0..1 in 0.05 steps walks the strands smoothly through the same crossfade the auto mode animates, wrapping so that 0.00 and 1.00 are byte-identical.
dials.portEffect: Same gating and same continuous wrap-around walk (0.00 == 1.00), with the same per-strand phase groupings. The mechanism matches; only the colours it walks through differ (see the grey vs cream observation).

feedback: Invert the twinkle. The original never brightens an individual pixel above its strand colour: its per-pixel twinkle is a momentary BLACKOUT — one bulb drops to 0,0,0 for a single frame (~0.05 s) and comes back. At untouched defaults that happens ~189 times a minute across 60 px, i.e. 0.16 blacked-out pixels present in any given frame. The port instead holds ~14 of 60 pixels boosted up to 4x for ~0.6 s each (~1533 onsets/min, 15.4 deviant px/frame). Aim for ~0.16 dark deviants per frame and zero bright deviants at default Twinkles.

Add the missing global flash. The original pulses the ENTIRE strip — all 60 pixels, same factor, same instant — from its base cap (raw 63) to full (raw 255) over a ~0.6 s ramp up and down, on a 33.0 s cadence at untouched defaults. The rate is driven by sliderTwinkles: 0/min at 0, 3/min at 0.5, 10.5/min at 1. The port has no such event at any Twinkles value. Note the original's boost source is per-frame and shared across pixels, not per pixel — that is exactly the split the port seems to have collapsed into a per-pixel term.

Fix two of the five strand colours. Held palette (AutoFadePalettes=0), 255-scaled: the warm strand should be a deep orange 255,45,0 (hue 11 deg), not the port's amber 255,138,0 (hue 32 deg); the pink strand should be a red-pink 255,0,77 (hue 342 deg), not the port's magenta 255,0,231 (hue 306 deg). Red 255,0,0, green ~0..4,255,0 and blue 0,~8,255 are already correct.

The warm strand's fade target is a NEUTRAL GREY, not a warm cream. In the original, sweeping ManualPaletteSelect (AutoFade=0) takes the deep-orange strand down to raw 24,19,24 (~98,78,98 of 255, a desaturated grey) at v=0.65 and back; the port's amber strand barely moves (raw 57,46,33 at the same point, minimum raw 51,36,14 anywhere in the sweep). This is likely the same grey template entry other Christmas-family patterns in this corpus carry.

Overall level is ~1.9x too hot at defaults (mean brightness 40.7 vs 21.6). Roughly 3/4 of that is the excess bright twinkles; the remaining ~24% (25.7 vs 20.7 with Twinkles=0) will follow from the two palette corrections above.

sliderCycleTime's range is shifted: the original spans 5.6 s (v=0) to 34.5 s (v=1); the port spans 3.0 s to 30.6 s. The default renders already agree at ~15 s, so this is a range/offset correction, not a rate bug — raise the port's floor by ~2.6 s and its ceiling by ~4 s.

The strand-to-pixel assignment should be a deterministic near-balanced spread, not a random draw. The original produces group sizes 62/61/60/59/58 at 300 px and 3/3/2/2/2 at 12 px; the port produces 67/61/61/56/55 and 4/3/2/2/1. The two agree at the default 60 px (14/13/12/11/10) by coincidence, so this only shows on off-default rigs.

Everything else is already right and should not be disturbed: the 5-strand structure, fixed strand membership, the base brightness cap (raw 63 of 255), the ~15 s crossfade period at defaults, the per-strand fade phase groupings (green+blue dip together, red dips half a cycle later), the AutoFadePalettes gate threshold, the ManualPaletteSelect wrap at 0/1, control names and kinds, and time-based (fps-invariant) animation.
